9/5/11; Columbus, OH; Nationwide Arena
Raw SuperShow 9/5/11 – Labor Day – featured an opening in-ring segment in which CM Punk came out, sat in the ring, and said he was different – he spoke differently, he walked differently – and that tends to piss people off; Punk then mentioned he was facing R-Truth later in the show but would rather kick Kevin Nash in the face; he went on to say Nash had the same music since 1996 and the same dyed hair since the first Gulf War, adding he knew Nash and Triple H were still best buddies; moments later, Punk called for Nash to come out and face him like a man, with Nash eventually walking out to the entrance stage and saying he does what he wants when he wants; Punk followed by mentioning every gimmick Nash has had, including Super Shredder, and said Nash won his first world title the same year Justin Bieber was born and Punk couldn’t yet legally drive; as Nash approached the ring, Triple H came out, with Nash telling Triple H to get rid of Punk; Triple H then entered the ring and said he got footage from security at the Staples Center; Triple H then said Nash himself was responsible for sending the text, as he was caught going into Triple H’s locker room at the same time he supposedly got the text; Nash then admitted to sending the text, saying he made the WWE cool again; Triple H agreed it was time to get rid of somebody, and implied it would be Nash; after Nash discussed pushing Triple H the previous week, and did so again, Triple H decked him and told him he was fired before then leaving the ring; Punk then pointed and laughed at Nash before saying “Best of luck in your future endevours;” following the commercial break, John Laurinaitis was shown leaving in a limo with Nash; included footage of WWE World Champion Alberto Del Rio and Ricardo Rodriguez arriving to the arena; featured the announcement The Rock surpassed 1 million followers on Twitter, with Jerry Lawler then saying Survivor Series “would be electrifying;” included a backstage segment with Drew McIntyre and Christian in which they talked about wanting title shots, with Del Rio and Rodriguez then walking in and Del Rio trying to talk Christian into taking out John Cena, saying it was Cena’s fault he lost to World Heavyweight Champion Randy Orton the previous week on Smackdown; featured an ad promoting ‘Inside Out,’ staring Triple H; featured a “Did you know?” graphic which read WWE has more Facebook fans than the NFL, NHL, NASCAR, MLB, UFC, Pepsi, and Nike; included Wade Barrett talking backstage with Tyler Reks and Curt Hawkins, with Del Rio and Rodriguez walking in and trying to talk Barrett into taking out Cena; featured an ad promoting the WWE Network, coming in 2012; included a backstage segment with Del Rio, alongside Rodriguez, and WWE US Champion Dolph Ziggler, with Del Rio trying to talk Ziggler into taking out Cena; after Ziggler made a comment about Del Rio not being at the show the previous week, Nikki & Brie Bella walked up to ADR fawning over him; Del Rio then told Ziggler that maybe Vickie Guerrero wasn’t looking at Jack Swagger to add to her stable but because she wanted someone to fight for her; featured footage of Sheamus speaking to a school in Bridgeport, CT about not being a bully; included a backstage segment with Zack Ryder celebrating with Cena, as Ryder filmed for ‘Z: True Long Island Story;’ during the segment, Cena made fun of those who wear their sunglasses indoors, a subtle remark directed towards the Rock; featured an ad promoting ‘Randy Orton: The Evolution of a Predator;’ included a “Did you know?” graphic which read Super Smackdown Live was the #1 primetime show on all of cable TV:
WWE Tag Team Champions Kofi Kingston & Evan Bourne defeated Jinder Mahal & the Great Khali in a non-title match at 3:15 when Bourne pinned Mahal with the Air Bourne after Khali accidentally chopped Mahal in the head when Kofi moved out of the way
Beth Phoenix (w/ Natalya Neidhart) pinned Eve with the Glam Slam at 2:03; WWE Divas Champion Kelly Kelly and Natalya provided guest commentary for the bout; stipulations stated the winner would challenge Kelly at Night of Champions; after the contest, Natalya jumped Kelly from behiind on the floor before joining Beth in the ring
CM Punk pinned R-Truth (w/ Mike Mizanin) with the Go To Sleep at 9:45; during his entrance, Truth cut a promo on Punk calling himself different, with Truth saying he has been speaking the truth his entire life; Truth then said maybe he needed to be a good R-Truth and buy a ticket to Night of Champions; moments later, Miz joined him, said Triple H wasn’t doing his job right, and set up a match for he and Truth to face WWE Tag Team Champions Evan Bourne & Kofi Kingston at Night of Champions; during the match, it was noted Miz would soon host a Sirius radio show; during the final minute of the contest, Miz was ejected after the referee caught him grabbing Punk’s foot from the floor; after the match, Triple H walked out to the ring, with Punk taking the mic and saying he didn’t buy that Triple H and Kevin Nash were at odds; Triple H followed by saying he didn’t care and he had changed their match to a No DQ match, adding he would hurt Punk and might fire him too; Punk stopped Triple H from leaving, calling him the “Cerebral AssAssin,” and adding that if Punk wins, Triple H has to resign as COO; Triple H agreed and left the ring
Jerry Lawler & Zack Ryder (mystery partner) defeated David Otunga & Michael McGillicutty at 2:08 when Ryder pinned Otunga with the Rough Ryder after Lawler hit the fistdrop off the top; during his entrance, Lawler cut a promo saying he never said his opponents weren’t good athletes, just that they didn’t have any charisma; he then added his tag team partner had a lot of it, with a video montage then airing of Ryder
World Heavyweight Champion Randy Orton pinned Heath Slater in a non-title match with the RKO at 2:56
John Cena, John Morrison, Sheamus, & Alex Riley defeated Wade Barrett, Christian, Jack Swagger, & WWE US Champion Dolph Ziggler in an impromptu elimination match at around the 19-minute mark; prior to the bout, Cena cut an in-ring promo in which he called out WWE World Champion Alberto Del Rio, with ADR saying he was not in the ring because he was protecting Cena; he then called for “the rudos of Raw” to appear, with Ziggler, Barrett, Christian, Swagger, attacking Cena; moments later, Riley, Morrison, and Sheamus ran out to make the save, with Teddy Long then setting up an immediate match; Swagger forced Morrison to submit to the ankle lock at around the 4-minute mark after Morrison sustained Ziggler’s sleeper; moments later, Vickie Guerrero appeared ringside; Swagger forced Riley to submit with the ankle lock at around the 10-minute mark after a bomb off the ropes; Sheamus pinned Barrett with the boot to the face at around the 13:30 mark; Christian and Sheamus fought to a double count-out at around the 15-minute mark when Sheamus chased Christian into the crowd and then up the ramp; late in the match, there were dueling chants of “Let’s go Cena” and “Cena sucks;” Cena pinned Ziggler with the FU at around the 19-minute mark after Ziggler tagged himself into the bout; Cena forced Swagger to submit with the STFU after reversing the ankle lock; after the match, Del Rio attempted to attack Cena but Cena fought him off (the bout began during the commercial break)

9/19/11; Cleveland, OH; Quicken Loans Arena
9/19/11 – featured an opening in-ring promo by CM Punk in which he noted Cleveland had never been kind to him, noting Bob Holly punched him hard in the eye, he had to give up the World Heavyweight Title in 2008, and his pride was now hurting after losing to Triple H in their No DQ match at Night of Champions; Punk then said R-Truth and Mike Mizanin were right that there was a conspiracy in the WWE, just not the one they speak of; as he continued, Triple H interrupted, gave Punk credit for their war, and said Alberto Del Rio deserved his rematch against WWE World Champion John Cena but Punk also deserved a title rematch; Triple H then said Punk, Cena, and Del Rio would compete for the title at Hell in a Cell inside the cell; moments later, Triple H said he had nothing to do with everything that’s been happening to Punk lately, then taking off his jacket in case Punk wanted to fight some more; Punk replied by saying someone was playing both of them to their own advantage; John Laurinaitis then walked out, saying it’s gone too far and Punk was in the middle of the conspiracy; Punk then said Laurinaitis was behind it all because he wanted Triple H’s job, he was the one that sent Truth and Miz to the ring, and cut his mic the previous week; Laurinaitis then reminded Punk that he worked for him and he wouldn’t be disrespected, with Triple H then reminding Laurinaitis that he worked for him and then said he would get to the bottom of it; Laurinaitis then fired Punk, with Punk laughing it off before Triple H said Punk wasn’t fired; Triple H then said he would get to the bottom of things and someone would be fired; included a backstage segment in which Triple H told Chad Patton he wanted to see Miz and Truth the moment they arrived to the arena; moments later, ADR complained to Triple H about being put in Hell in a Cell, with Triple H offering to take away ADR’s title shot altogether; featured an ad promoting ‘Inside Out,’ staring Triple H; included a “Did you know?” graphic which read WWE programming is shown each week to 145 countries and in 30 different languages; featured an in-ring segment in which Justin Roberts introduced Hugh Jackman, who discussed hosting the Oscars but it not being anything like Raw; as Jackman discussed his new movie ‘Real Steel,’ Vickie Guerrero interrupted, alongside WWE US Champion Dolph Ziggler; moments later, Vickie began hitting on Jackman, saying she was his biggest fan; moments later, Ziggler went off on Jackman, saying Ziggler didn’t interrupt him on the set of ‘Batman;’ Ziggler then said he beat three superstars, not robots – then adding “No offense, Mason Ryan;” after Ziggler and Jackman shared words, Jackman said he would find the biggest underdog backstage and help them beat Ziggler in the ring; the crowd then chanted “We want Ryder,” with Jackman taking a sign from a fan that read “Ryder > Wolverine” and showing it off to the crowd; included a backstage segment with Miz, Truth, and Laurinaitis in which Laurinaitis said Triple H wanted to see them, then both apologizing to Laurinaitis for their behavior the previous night; featured a backstage segment with Triple H, Miz, and Truth in which Miz apologized for attacking the referee and interfering in his match, with Truth then apologizing to Triple H, the WWE Universe, and all the Little Jimmys; Truth then said they would never do anything like that again and wanted nothing more than to be WWE superstars, then adding they thought Triple H was doing a great job as COO; Triple H then accepted their apology, then finding them both $250,000 apiece for attacking an official; Triple H then added they would face Punk and Cena later in the show; included an in-ring segment in which Jim Ross announced Randy Orton would challenge World Heavyweight Champion Mark Henry at Hell in a Cell, after being told of the announcement by Teddy Long; moments later, Henry came out for an in-ring interview with Ross about accomplishing his goal after 15 years and facing Orton in Hell in a Cell; Henry then said he would never forgive the fans because they never supported him, then telling Ross to apologize for them and for himself not believing in Henry; moments later, Ross apologized, with Henry grabbing him by the tie until Jerry Lawler left the broadcast table to try to talk Henry into letting Ross go; moments later, Henry let go only to grab Lawler; Lawler threw several punches but was quickly beaten down and sustained the powerslam; Henry then took Lawler to the floor and powerslammed him through the announce table; following the commercial break, Lawler was helped backstage by referees as Josh Matthews took over for him on commentary; featured a backstage segment with Jackman and Zack Ryder in which Jackman talked about how much of an underdog Ryder was before the two then got ready for Ryder’s match; included an ad promoting ‘OMG: The Top 50 Incidents in WWE History;’ featured a ‘Did you know?’ graphic which read Cena has 8,642,160 Facebook fans, more than the Rock, Tiger Woods, Jennifer Lopez, Dwayne Wade, Kim Kardashian, Tony Hawk, Sarah Palin, the Dalai Lama, and Johnny Depp; included a look at Jackman’s ‘Real Steel;’ featured a vignette on Jack Swagger; moments later, Swagger caught Vickie watching the video, with Swagger saying he was much better than Ziggler; Vickie then said she would be proud to have Swagger in her stable; Swagger then walked past Ziggler, still holding his face from being punched by Jackman; included a backstage segment with Punk and Cena talking about their tag team match later in the show and facing off against ADR at Hell in a Cell; featured a video package on the history of Hell in a Cell:
